name: James Landay
title: Denning Director of Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, Anand Rajaraman and Venky Harinarayan Professor and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
research_topics: User modeling from everyday computer use
Digital biomarkers and mobile/ubiquitous health sensing
Interaction and user interface design tools
Design metaphors and ontologies in AI-assisted design
current_direction: LLM health coaches that preserve user agency (Bloom, GPTCoach)
Just-in-time objective inference to specialize AI interfaces
Inferring long-horizon life goals from everyday computer-use traces
Multimodal LLM agents for accessibility (blind/low-vision video)
Digital biomarkers from passive sensing for neurodegenerative disease
current_direction_basis: Driven by the 2025-2026 evidence collected here, not by his older biography. Two CHI 2026 papers set the frame: 'Bloom' (LLM-augmented behavior change, with Joerke/Sapkota/Brunskill/King) and 'Just-In-Time Objectives' (with Michelle Lam, Shaikh, Yang, Heer, Bernstein). The May 2026 arXiv preprint 'What Are You Really Trying to Do?' extends the coaching line from in-the-moment activity to inferred life goals. 'Making Videos Accessible... Multimodal Agent Video Player' (arXiv, Feb 2026) is the accessibility-agent thread. 'A framework of digital biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases' (Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Apr 2026, with Fei-Fei/Adeli) is the sensing-for-health thread. CHI 2025's GPTCoach is the direct predecessor of Bloom. The Spring 2026 Stanford HCI Seminar lineup corroborates: his advisees Michelle Lam, Matthew Joerke and Nava Haghighi gave talks on exactly these topics.

evidence.title: Just-In-Time Objectives: A General Approach for Specialized AI Interactions
evidence.summary: CHI 2026 paper (issued 2026-04-13). Crossref-verified authors: Michelle S. Lam, Omar Shaikh, Hallie Xu, Alice Guo, Diyi Yang, Jeffrey Heer, James A. Landay, Michael S. Bernstein. OpenAlex abstract: 'Large language models promise a broad set of functions, but when not given a specific objective, they default to generic results. We demonstrate that inferring the user's in-the-moment objective, then rapidly optimizing for that singular objective, enables LLMs to produce specialized tools, interfaces, and responses.'
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

evidence.title: Bloom: Designing for LLM-Augmented Behavior Change Interactions
evidence.summary: CHI 2026 paper (issued 2026-04-13). Crossref-verified authors: Matthew Joerke, Defne Genc, Valentin Teutschbein, Shardul Sapkota, Sarah Chung, Paul Schmiedmayer, Maria Ines Campero, Abby C. King, Emma Brunskill, James A. Landay. OpenAlex abstract: 'Large language models (LLMs) offer novel opportunities to support health behavior change, yet existing work has narrowly focused on text-only interactions... we present Bloom, an application for physical activity promotion that integrates an LLM-based health coaching chatbot with existing design strategies and UI elements.'
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

evidence.title: "What Are You Really Trying to Do?": Co-Creating Life Goals from Everyday Computer Use
evidence.summary: arXiv preprint dated 2026-05-01 (arXiv:2605.00497). OpenAlex-verified authors: Shardul Sapkota, Matthew Joerke, Zane Sabbagh, Omar Shaikh, Grace Wang, James A. Landay. Abstract: 'existing systems only capture what a person is doing in the moment -- not why they are doing it -- limiting these systems to surface-level support. We introduce striving co-creation, a process for inferring broader life goals from unstructured observations of co[mputer use].'

evidence.title: Making Videos Accessible for Blind and Low Vision Users Using a Multimodal Agent Video Player
evidence.summary: arXiv preprint dated 2026-02-04 (arXiv:2602.04104). OpenAlex-verified authors: Adriana Olmos, Anoop Kumar Sinha, Renelito Delos Santos, Ruben Rodriguez Rodriguez, James A. Landay, Sam Sepah, Philip Nelson, Shaun K. Kane. Abstract: 'we introduce a prototype that leverages a multimodal agent - powered by a novel conversational architecture using a multimodal large language model (MLLM) - to provide BLV users with an interactive, accessible video experience.'

evidence.title: A framework of digital biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases
evidence.summary: Journal article issued 2026-04-23. Crossref-verified authors include Favour Nerrise, Narayan Schutz, Qingyu Zhao, Arnold Milstein, Kevin Schulman, Victor W. Henderson, James Landay, Li Fei-Fei, Feng Vankee Lin, Ehsan Adeli. Places Landay in the passive-sensing / digital-health-measurement line of work alongside Stanford HAI colleagues.

evidence.title: GPTCoach: Towards LLM-Based Physical Activity Coaching
evidence.summary: CHI 2025 paper (issued 2025-04-25). Crossref-verified authors: Matthew Joerke, Shardul Sapkota, Lyndsea Warkenthien, Niklas Vainio, Paul Schmiedmayer, Emma Brunskill, James A. Landay. Direct predecessor of the CHI 2026 Bloom paper; establishes the LLM-health-coaching agenda that the 2026 work builds on.
evidence.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

evidence.title: Spring 2026 Stanford HCI Seminar talks by Landay-advised students
evidence.summary: The Stanford HCI Seminar page lists, for Spring 2026: '15 May Nava Haghighi, Stanford University, Toward Ontological Multiplicity in AI and Computing'; '22 May Michelle Lam, Stanford University, Just-in-Time Objectives for Specialized AI Interactions'; '29 May Matthew Joerke, Stanford University, Promoting Agency in Human-AI Interaction: Insights from AI Health Coaching'. The Stanford Profiles page lists Haghighi and Joerke as Landay's doctoral dissertation advisees and Lam as a co-advisee. Confirms the group is actively presenting this work in 2026.

evidence.title: 2025-26 teaching: CS 147, CS 147L, CS 146
evidence.summary: Stanford Profiles lists under '2025-26 Courses': 'Cross-platform Mobile App Development CS 147L (Aut)', 'Game Development CS 146 (Win)', 'Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction Design CS 147 (Aut)'. CS 147 is the undergraduate-facing intro HCI course the HCI Group's own connect page points undergraduates toward, making it the most natural first point of contact with Landay.

undergrad_signals.signal: Listed as supervisor for 'Supervised Undergraduate Research CS 195 (Aut, Win, Spr, Sum)' under Independent Studies on his official Stanford Profiles page
undergrad_signals.note: Quoted verbatim from the 'Independent Studies (14)' block: 'Supervised Undergraduate Research CS 195 (Aut, Win, Spr, Sum)'. This is the standard Stanford CS mechanism for undergraduate research credit and is offered in all four quarters. It confirms he is set up to supervise undergrad research, but it is a catalog affiliation, not an announcement that he currently has openings.

undergrad_signals.note: Same Independent Studies block lists: 'Senior Project CS 191 (Aut, Win, Spr)', 'Writing Intensive Senior Research Project CS 191W (Aut, Win, Spr)', 'Independent Work CS 199 (Aut, Win, Spr, Sum)', 'Independent Work CS 199P (Aut, Win, Spr, Sum)', and 'Independent Study SYMSYS 196 (Aut, Win, Spr, Sum)'. The group does list 30+ named PhD and post-doc students. Treat this as a neutral-to-negative signal: the site has the category but does not publish undergrad names.

undergrad_signals.signal: Non-Stanford undergraduate interns are explicitly declined
undergrad_signals.note: Quoted: 'Non-Stanford students interested in internships Generally speaking, we do not have the resources for non-Stanford interns. We will not respond to internship requests from students. If you have research experience in HCI, and are interested in a project related to our group's work, please have a faculty member at your university email me, and have them include an explanation of your particular qualifications for HCI research.' This matters for targeting: the undergrad pathway here is realistically Stanford-internal.

undergrad_signals.signal: No mention of CURIS anywhere on any page fetched in this task
undergrad_signals.note: Searched landay.org, profiles.stanford.edu/james-landay, hci.stanford.edu (home, people, connect, research, seminar) for 'CURIS' - zero hits. Absence of evidence only; CURIS participation is not ruled out, it is simply not documented on the pages fetched.

recruiting.statement: No Landay-specific recruiting or 'join us' statement was found on any page fetched. The closest group-level statements on the Stanford HCI Group connect page are restrictive rather than open: 'Non-Stanford students interested in internships Generally speaking, we do not have the resources for non-Stanford interns. We will not respond to internship requests from students.' and, on graduate applications, 'Can I discuss my application with you? No. (So that the faculty can spend their time with current students, teaching, and doing research.)' The only conditionally-open statement is for post-docs, not undergraduates: 'Can I do a Post-Doc with the HCI Group? When there's a great fit, a talented student, and funding, the HCI Group sometimes has Post-Doc positions.'

state_rationale: OUTREACH, not OPENING. The lab is unambiguously active: two CHI 2026 papers, two 2026 arXiv preprints, a 2026 Nature Reviews Bioengineering article, a CHI 2025 paper, and three Spring 2026 HCI Seminar talks by his own advisees. Landay is also listed on his official Stanford profile as supervising 'Supervised Undergraduate Research CS 195', 'Senior Project CS 191/191W' and 'Independent Work CS 199' in all quarters, and he teaches the undergraduate gateway course CS 147 in Autumn 2025-26. That is a strong, real undergraduate pathway. But it does not meet the OPENING bar: nothing fetched is an explicit, currently-open undergraduate position or program announcement - the CS 195/191/199 entries are standing course-catalog supervision affiliations available across Stanford CS, not a posted opening. Counter-signals were also found: the HCI Group people page's 'Masters Students, Undergraduates, Interns' section is commented out (no undergrads listed), the connect page declines to discuss applications, and it explicitly refuses non-Stanford intern requests. Net: a Stanford undergraduate is well-positioned for a cold email - ideally via CS 147 or a CS 195/191 proposal anchored to the LLM-health-coaching or just-in-time-objectives line - but there is no advertised opening to point to.
